# Regions of neptune.b33 identified as something other than code, for
# apple2tc's --coverage report.
#
# Format: "FROM TO name", addresses hexadecimal with an optional '$' prefix,
# '#' starts a comment.
#
# Deciding that bytes are data is a conclusion about the program, not something
# the disassembler can derive, so every line here needs its evidence. The
# coverage report flags any range that the disassembler also reached as code,
# which is the check that these claims stay true.

# --- hi-res drawing tables -------------------------------------------------
# Read as a pair at $3878/$387D, which builds a ($00) pointer from them:
#
#   3878: LDA $0C00,Y   ; -> $01, the HIGH byte
#   387D: LDA $0D00,Y   ; -> $00, the LOW byte
#
# so $0C00 is the high table and $0D00 the low one, and not the other way
# round. Combined, entries 0..191 reproduce the standard hi-res row address
# base + (r&7)*$400 + ((r>>3)&7)*$80 + (r>>6)*$28 for base $4000 -- all 192 of
# them, exactly, and none of them for base $2000. That is the derivation, and
# it also settles which page this game draws on. Entries past 191 are $FF00
# filler, so the tables are declared as 192 bytes rather than 256.
0C00 0CBF tbl_hgr_row_hi
0D00 0DBF tbl_hgr_row_lo

# --- the screen ------------------------------------------------------------
# Hi-res page 2 is the framebuffer, on three independent grounds:
#   - it is the displayed page (vid_control $0C at the capture point),
#   - the row tables above decode to exactly this range, and
#   - of the 184 pages of $0800-$BFFF, 160 are byte-identical to sectors of
#     dsk/Neptune.dsk and the only 24 that differ are inside $4100-$5FFF --
#     i.e. the game has drawn on this and on nothing else.
# The writes agree: the indexed store bases in the code include $4350, $4750,
# $4B50, $4F50, $5350, $5750 and $5B50, spaced exactly $400 apart, which is the
# hi-res interleave.
4000 5FFF hgr_page2_framebuffer

# --- NOT declared, and why -------------------------------------------------
#
# $6000-$ABFF, the largest unknown span. It contains data -- $65F0 is read as
# an indexed base by the sprite-erase routine at $3884, and $9F00 by fourteen
# more sites -- but the *extents* have not been derived, only the bases, and a
# range guessed from a base is exactly the kind of claim this file exists to
# not make. Bit-7 density varies across it ($8000-$8FFF is 2.1%, consistent
# with 7-bit shape data; $A000-$ABFF is 38%), which suggests more than one kind
# of content rather than one table to declare.
#
# $BB00-$BFFF is code, not data, and declaring it here would be a lie. It is a
# Disk II driver plus language-card and message text that Neptune's loader
# blitted in from stale disk sectors; six probes across $BC57-$BF67 fired zero
# times in a 3000-frame disk boot, against controls that fired 630 and 2 times.
# So it is unreachable code, which the coverage report should keep reporting as
# unidentified rather than have hidden behind a data declaration.
